angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 505,078 km at 68.67 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.5622 +/- 0.0147 mas (same row, RUWE 1.22): 68.67 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.726 +/- 0.007 solar radii from Wilson et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1064 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511.1043W/abstract): 505,078 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.748 +/- 0.032 solar masses from Wilson et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1064 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511.1043W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4734 +/- 67 K from Wilson et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1064 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511.1043W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Wilson et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1064 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.511.1043W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1064.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.590, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
